item.research_question: How does substituting Cr with V to tune atomic volume misfit affect the magnetic order and electric transport properties (specifically strange metallicity) in the CoNi(Cr/V) medium-entropy alloy system?
item.material_system: Ternary equiatomic CoNiCr (CNC), CoNi(Cr0.5V0.5) (CNCV), and CoNiV (CNV) medium-entropy alloys
item.processing_route: Arc melting of high-purity elements, homogenization at 1100 °C for 24 hrs in Ar followed by water quenching, cold rolling to ~75% thickness reduction, and solutionizing at 1000 °C for 60 min followed by water quenching
item.test_conditions: Magnetization and electrical transport measurements performed in the temperature range of 5–335 K using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) and 4-probe method
key_findings: All three compositions exhibited a single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure with lattice parameters of 3.576 ± 0.004 Å (CNC), 3.598 ± 0.002 Å (CNCV), and 3.617 ± 0.002 Å (CNV).
Magnetic moments at 5 K were extremely small: 0.005 μB/f.u. for CNC, 0.007 μB/f.u. for CNCV, and 0.002 μB/f.u. for CNV.
The CoNiCr system displayed linear temperature dependence of resistivity (ρ(T) = ρ0 + ρ1 T), indicative of strange metallicity.
Vanadium-substituted samples (CNCV and CNV) required an additional electron-electron scattering term (ρ2 T2) to fit resistivity data, suggesting a deviation from pure quantum criticality.
Coercive fields for all alloys ranged from 30 to 60 Gauss (2.4–4.8 kA/m), classifying them as semihard magnets.
Residual resistivity ratio (RRR) monotonically decreased with increasing Vanadium substitution, indicating higher residual resistivity.
No significant magnetoresistance was observed in any of the samples.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the small magnetic moments and strange metallicity to magnetically driven chemical short-range order (SRO) and magnetic frustration. They propose that complex interactions between ferromagnetic Co/Ni and antiferromagnetic Cr/V create unbalanced magnetic sublattices (ferrimagnetism), where the frustration of magnetic moments leads to the observed linear resistivity and quantum critical behavior.
item.limitations: The ferrimagnetic Curie temperature was not determined due to setup limitations preventing high-temperature measurements, and the authors note that direct experimental evidence of SRO remains intangible without advanced tools like muon spin resonance.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that careful experimental tools such as muon spin resonance and/or neutron reflectivity are needed to shed light on the magnetic short-range order driven by a state of frustration.
quotes: The electric transport measurements revealed a strange metallicity evidenced through the observation of the linear temperature dependence of the resistivity.

These moments were dramatically lower than the individual moments or constituent elements, which implied the presence of counteracting complex magnetic interactions, as expected in ferrimagnetic or antiferromagnetic states.
Careful experimental tools, such as muon spin resonance and/or neutron reflectivity, would shed light on this magnetic SRO driven by a state of frustration.
